question: A shopkeeper sells an item at 20% discount on the marked price and earns a profit of 90%. If he sells the same item at 40% discount, then his new profit percentage will be:
solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper sells an item at 20% discount on the marked price and earns a profit of 90%. If he sells the same item at 40% discount, then his new profit percentage will be:

**Formula used:**

Let Marked Price (MP) = 100

Discount = 20%

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit%)

New Discount = 40%

New Selling Price (NSP) = MP - New Discount

New Profit % = (NSP - CP) / CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Let Marked Price (MP) = 100

Discount = 20%

Selling Price (SP) = 100 - 20 = 80

Profit = 90%

Cost Price (CP) = 80 / 1.90

⇒ CP = 42.105

New Discount = 40%

New Selling Price (NSP) = 100 - 40 = 60

New Profit % = (60 - 42.105) / 42.105 × 100

⇒ New Profit % = 17.895 / 42.105 × 100

⇒ New Profit % ≈ 42.5%

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**
